title: Dawn processions
hookLine: before Guru Nanak's gurpurab, sangats sing through the streets at dawn
tomorrow: the procession is coming down your street. what does your family do?

lines: AN ALARM SET TO KEEP THINGS QUIET.
WHY A HYMN AT THE DOOR?
cards: An early alarm is usually set to keep a house quiet: phone on low, nobody else woken. So here's an odd one. In the weeks before Guru Nanak's gurpurab, some sangats gather before sunrise and walk the neighborhood singing.
Not inside the gurdwara. Down ordinary streets, stopping at front doors where a porch light is on and a tray of tea is waiting. Why would anyone carry a hymn to someone's door in the dark?

teach.b: The name holds half the answer. Prabhat is the dawn. Pheri is a round, a walk that comes back to where it began.
A prabhat pheri is a dawn round: the sangat walks a loop of homes, singing, and the homes on the route open up.

teach.h: A DOOR OPENS, A HYMN, AN ARDAS.
teach.b: A family asks the pheri to stop at their door; they join a hymn and an Ardas, then send the singers on with tea or something sweet. Now the other half. The hour isn't random.
Guru Nanak names it in the fourth pauri of the Japji: amrit vela sach naao vaddiaaee veechaar. In the ambrosial hour before dawn, the true Name, and reflection on its greatness.
The Granth even keeps a raga for this hour, Prabhati. So the puzzle turns around. The pheri isn't there to wake the street.
It brings the early hour, the one Sikhs keep for the Name, to the door of anyone who wants it.
And it walks toward a day: Guru Nanak's gurpurab. Bhai Gurdas wrote that when Guru Nanak appeared, the mist cleared and light spread through the world.
A pheri walks that picture through the streets, singing in the dark until the light comes up behind it.

how: In the days before Guru Nanak's gurpurab, some sangats hold prabhat pheris: small groups walk a route of homes before dawn singing shabads, and families who host them join an Ardas and offer tea or sweets.

o: a morning run held by the gurdwara youth group
the evening prayer sung at home before sleeping
a dawn round of hymns, door to door, before a gurpurab

games.q: the dawn round — tap the pairs.
p: a round that comes back where it began
the hour before dawn, in the Japji's pauri 4
the Granth's raga for the dawn

s: a prabhat pheri is the big daytime procession
that's the nagar kirtan. the pheri is a smaller dawn round of homes.
the Japji names the hour before dawn for the true Name
amrit vela sach naao: the ambrosial hour, the true Name, in pauri 4.
the pheri is meant to wake up the whole neighborhood
it stops where a family asks it in: a visit at the door, not an alarm.

games.q: your neighbor, who isn't Sikh, hears soft singing outside before dawn and asks what's going on. what's the honest answer?
o: a prabhat pheri: a dawn round of hymns before Guru Nanak's gurpurab, stopping where invited.
a nagar kirtan: the big procession, which always starts in the dark.
a wake-up call, so everyone gets to the gurdwara on time.
games.why: prabhat is dawn and pheri a round: the sangat brings the Japji's early hour to the doors that ask for it, in the days before the gurpurab.

practice: If you know a line of Gurbani, or just the word Waheguru, say it softly, almost a hum, one round for each breath. Keep it quiet enough that nobody else in the house would wake.
When you lose the thread, simply start the round again, like a pheri coming back past the same door.

wordCard.voice: Prabhat pheri. A dawn round: the sangat walking and singing from door to door before sunrise, in the days before a gurpurab.

orig.note: Punjabi: prabhat, dawn; pheri, a round. a dawn round of hymns before a gurpurab.

carryVoice: Carry this: singing at dawn, a hymn brought to the door before the day begins. Day 1752, and the tea is still hot.
